title: Commodity prices to hit record highs before easing through 2027
gist: Oxford Economics forecasts the S&P GSCI to hit a record in Q4 2026 (+28% annual average in 2026) on a Middle East energy shock, with Brent above $100 through Q2 2027 and a divergent outlook across gas, gold, base metals and grains.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts the S&P GSCI spot index to rise 28% in annual-average terms in 2026 and reach a record high in Q4 2026, driven primarily by energy and spreading as fuel, electricity and transport costs feed into other commodities.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Commodity-complex peak is expected near year-end, followed by gradual easing through 2027.

insights.claim: The central forecast is for aggregate commodity prices to decline gradually through 2027 as Middle Eastern exports recover, but the pace depends on how quickly physical supply is restored and whether geopolitical risks subside.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Supply normalisation speed is the key swing factor.

insights.claim: Brent is now expected to average above $100 per barrel through Q2 2027 after attacks on Red Sea export infrastructure and a persistent risk premium, converging to a long-run ~$60 equilibrium by 2029 rather than 2028.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Delayed normalisation raises inflation persistence and central-bank hawkishness risk.

insights.claim: September's attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carried about 4 million barrels per day and let Saudi exports bypass the Strait of Hormuz, showed the vulnerability of alternative export routes; as capacity recovers the main obstacle to normalisation is the geopolitical risk premium rather than physical supply.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Prices could stay high even with adequate barrels; risk premium trades dominate.

insights.claim: Tight refined product markets have pushed European diesel refining spreads close to $100 per barrel, transmitting the energy shock to diesel-intensive mining, agricultural machinery and freight.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Refining margins and diesel costs are the transmission channel into other commodities.

insights.claim: Qatar and the UAE accounted for around 20% of global LNG trade pre-conflict but exports have been effectively trapped inside the Strait of Hormuz since March, leaving LNG-linked gas prices in Europe and Asia about 130% above pre-conflict levels versus a 45% rise in Brent.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: LNG is harder to reroute than crude; gas is more stressed than oil.

insights.claim: European gas inventories are the lowest for this time of year in over a decade, with baseline storage falling to 17% of capacity by 1 April 2027; a cold spell plus US LNG or Norwegian disruption could push prices toward $35/MMBtu while a mild winter could cap the peak near $21/MMBtu.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Weather-dependent binary: $21-$35/MMBtu range for winter peak.

insights.claim: Europe is better positioned than in 2021-22: gas demand is around a fifth below its 2021 level and LNG import capacity has expanded.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Limits the extreme-tail risk relative to the last energy crisis.

insights.claim: Gold has not benefited from the Middle East shock as much as expected because higher oil prices revived inflation concerns and tighter US policy expectations, supporting yields and the dollar; Oxford still expects gold to average $4,515/oz in 2026, $4,840 in 2027 and $5,140 in 2028 on central-bank and investor demand.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Structural gold uptrend underpinned by EM central-bank reserve diversification; expects fewer Fed hikes than markets price.

insights.claim: High silver prices are encouraging recycling and substitution in solar, constrained mine supply supports platinum, and palladium faces weaker structural demand as internal-combustion vehicles lose share.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Precious metals divergence: platinum supportive, palladium structurally weak.

insights.claim: Copper and aluminium should decline in early 2027 as disruptions ease and trade distortions unwind, but stay near historically high levels and strengthen later in 2027 on grids, electrification and data-centre demand plus constrained supply.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Dip-then-recovery shape; buy-the-dip case from structural demand.

insights.claim: Around 80% of exchange copper inventories are concentrated in the US as import-tariff expectations pulled metal there, so clarity on tariff policy could ease tightness elsewhere and put downward pressure on prices.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: US tariff clarity is a near-term bearish catalyst for copper prices and ex-US tightness.

insights.claim: Grain prices are expected to stay broadly stable through 2027 as comfortable inventories absorb risks from Black Sea port attacks, a strong El Niño, and higher energy costs, while fertiliser prices have eased as Gulf exports recovered and China relaxed export restrictions.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Agriculture is the lower-risk complex relative to energy.
